digest.component_or_area: store write lock / mkdir lock staleness detection
propositions: On platforms without /proc (e.g. macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant unsatisfiable and causing an unbounded lock wedge when a dead holder's pid is reused by an unrelated live process
The lock is treated as fresh whenever _pid_alive returns true, even on platforms where current_start cannot be determined, defeating the liveness proof and bypassing the 1h staleness ceiling

The fix applies _mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling to the live-pid branch only when current_start is None (unqualified verdict), while preserving immediate reclaim for proven-recycled pids (known differing start times)

A genuinely live owner cannot reach the staleness check because it still holds the exclusive fcntl leg, which a reclaimer would need to acquire first—the invariant ensures the ceiling fires only on orphans

The owner-identity and staleness logic was extracted from lock.py (798 LOC) to lock_owner.py to satisfy the 800 LOC module-size cap, with one-way dependency and all test references repointed to avoid silent breakage from re-export shims
